summary.intent: Fix a desktop E2E test issue and open a PR, then correct the commit type from fix(e2e) to chore(e2e) to avoid triggering unnecessary version bumps via release-please.
summary.outcome: PR #537 opened on github.com/FSM1/cipher-box, CI E2E workflow dispatched on the fix branch (~15 min run), and commit rewrote to chore(e2e) + force-pushed to prevent release-please from bumping sdk-core and other packages.

repo: Desktop E2E CI does not run automatically on PRs — it triggers only on main push or manual workflow_dispatch, so PR checks alone cannot confirm desktop E2E fixes.
release-please treats fix() commits as patch-level bumps and will version-bump every touched package (e.g. sdk-core); chore() commits are ignored by release-please.
The release-please bot can push a chore(release) commit to origin shortly after a PR is created, so force-with-lease must be used carefully and timing matters.

code.finding: Modified as part of the E2E fix; reachable by release-please version bumps when touched by fix() commits.
Same as .mts counterpart — dual .ts/.mts pattern in sdk-core scripts.
Desktop E2E scripts exist in both .ps1 (Windows) and .sh (Unix) variants for cross-platform CI.
Desktop E2E .ts helper — per existing memory, these .mjs/.ts helpers bypass tsc/eslint and bugs surface only deep in single-OS ci-e2e runs.
Shared E2E auth helper touched by this fix, suggesting auth setup was part of the broken test path.

workflow: Amend + git push --force-with-lease is safe when the bot has not yet pushed to origin; always check origin HEAD before rewording commits on shared branches.
Dispatching workflow_dispatch via gh CLI returns a run ID immediately; background monitoring with a ~15 min ETA is the right pattern for long E2E jobs.
Conventional commit type (fix vs chore) has direct release impact in monorepos using release-please — defaulting to chore for test/infra-only changes avoids unintended version bumps.

friction: fix(e2e) commit type caused release-please to queue version bumps across multiple packages including sdk-core before the user caught it.
Desktop E2E is not wired to PR triggers, meaning the standard PR review flow gives no CI signal for this class of fix without a manual workflow_dispatch.
open_items: CI E2E run 27889089548 was still in progress (~15 min) at end of session — result not yet confirmed.
PR #537 is open but not yet merged; merge is contingent on the E2E run going green.
Consider wiring desktop E2E to run on PRs (or at least on PRs touching tests/desktop-e2e/**) to avoid needing manual dispatch for every fix in this area.
